In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regenerative process of the red starfish E. sepositas is a complex phenomenon that is characterized by both morphallactic and re‐growth processes, which occur in a coordinated manner.
E. sepositis is a model organism for the study of the regenerative processes in starfish.
E. sepositis, as well as other echinoderms, are able to regenerate a wide spectrum of structures and tissues, including the skeleton, radial nerve cord and muscles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regenerative process can be considered a complex sequence of tissue and cell rearrangements, morphogenetic events, and differentiation processes.

E. sepositis arm regenerates are able to regenerate their amputated parts in a morphogenetic manner, with some direct re‐growth and some indirect re‐growth, with some morphallactic processes, with a relatively slow process, and with a high degree of differentiation.
E. sepositis shows a complex regenerative pattern, in which morphallactic and epimorphic phenomena are involved in a balanced way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regeneration process in E. sepositus is not a simple process of re‐growth, but is characterized by a complex series of morphogenetic and differentiation phenomena.
the red starfish E. sepositis is a good model for the study of regeneration processes in starfish.
, although starfish arm regeneration is a slow process, the overall process is very similar to the one described in other echinoderm classes.
